sub_question: SQ-3: CDH1 loss → PI3Ka → YAP convergent node in ILC CDK4/6i resistance

YAP nuclear CDH1 loss breast cancer lobular

mechanistic_finding.citation: Ouyang H et al. Oncogene. 2020 Aug;39(33):5570-5587.
mechanistic_finding.finding: E-cadherin (CDH1) cooperates with p190A RhoGAP to ACTIVATE LATS kinases → YAP phosphorylation and cytoplasmic sequestration (tumor suppression). CDH1 loss in ILC → LATS deactivation → YAP nuclear translocation → transcriptional co-activation (pro-tumorigenic).
mechanistic_finding.mechanism_arrow: CDH1 loss → LATS deactivation → YAP nuclear (confirmed in epithelial carcinoma context)
mechanistic_finding.breast_cancer_specific: NOT yet demonstrated in ILC breast cancer specifically — extrapolated from general epithelial carcinoma model
mechanistic_finding.status: MECHANISTIC_SUPPORT — CDH1→LATS→YAP chain established; ILC-specificity = novel claim

pi3k_yap_crosstalk.citation: Qian X et al. Acta Diabetol. 2021;58(1):23-33.
pi3k_yap_crosstalk.finding: YAP mediates interaction between Hippo and PI3K/AKT pathways. PI3K/AKT activation enhances YAP nuclear activity.
pi3k_yap_crosstalk.context: Diabetic nephropathy mesangial cells — not breast cancer
pi3k_yap_crosstalk.implication: PI3K→AKT→YAP amplification is a general cross-pathway mechanism. In ILC with CDH1 loss, BOTH CDH1-LATS (structural) AND PI3K-AKT (signaling) routes drive YAP nuclear activity.

synthesis.title: CDH1 loss in ILC drives YAP nuclear activity via DUAL routes
synthesis.route_1: CDH1 loss → LATS deactivation → YAP nuclear (PMID 32641858, structural/adherens junction mechanism)
synthesis.route_2: CDH1 loss → PI3Ka liberation → AKT → YAP nuclear amplification (PMID 32816106, signaling crosstalk)
synthesis.alpelisib_relevance: Alpelisib (PI3Ka inhibitor) suppresses Route 2 only. Route 1 (LATS deactivation) persists even with alpelisib. This LIMITS alpelisib's ability to fully suppress YAP nuclear activity — BUT does not affect alpelisib's CDK2 bypass benefit.
synthesis.combined_therapy_implication: Alpelisib + verteporfin (TEAD inhibitor) could target Route 2 (PI3K→YAP) + Route 1 (CDH1-LATS→YAP) simultaneously — comprehensive ILC YAP suppression
synthesis.this_is_separate_from_cdk46i_resistance: The CDH1→YAP axis is a separate tumor biology finding from the CDK4/6i resistance mechanism. It does NOT directly explain alpelisib benefit in CDK4/6i-progressed ILC, but suggests a third therapeutic vulnerability (YAP/TEAD inhibition) specific to CDH1-loss ILC.

impact_on_hypothesis.hyp_ilc_006_direct: NEUTRAL — CDH1→YAP does not strengthen or weaken the CDK4/6i resistance/alpelisib claim. The CDK4/6i resistance mechanism (CDH1→PI3Ka→AKT→CDK2 bypass) is independent of YAP.
impact_on_hypothesis.new_hypothesis_generated: hyp-ilc-009 candidate: CDH1 loss in ILC activates YAP via dual mechanism (LATS deactivation + PI3K-AKT crosstalk). YAP-TEAD inhibition (verteporfin, IAG933) should show ILC-specific efficacy greater than IDC. Co-treatment alpelisib+verteporfin may have synergy in CDH1-loss ILC.
impact_on_hypothesis.org_synthesis_validation: Validates organ synthesis conn-004 (YAP as ILC master regulator, confidence 0.74). The mechanistic underpinning (CDH1→LATS→YAP) is now established.

recommended_actions: Register hyp-ilc-009 (CDH1-LATS-YAP axis in ILC → TEAD inhibitor vulnerability) as new ACCEPT_MEDIUM candidate
Add verteporfin arm to ILC-EXP-004 preclinical protocol alongside alpelisib
